proposed_fixes.title: Validate drag-state lifetime against the supplied FancyZones crash
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: a monitor/work-area or dragged-window transition invalidates state during zone highlighting or snap completion. The public description does not establish a stack, and layout loss may be a separate symptom.
plan: Inspect the #33343 archive and extract the crash signature; establish whether it matches the older #13402 failure before combining them.
Trace the confirmed crash through src/modules/fancyzones/FancyZonesLib/FancyZones.cpp and its drag/snap state owners using the documented right-button Chrome sequence.

Check existing AbortMoveSize and destroyed-window guards on current main before proposing any equivalent guard. If the failure remains, correct only the newly demonstrated lifetime boundary and keep persisted layouts unchanged on failed snaps.
Add a regression for the actual failing transition; investigate restart/layout persistence separately if no common stack or state path connects it.
verification: Drag Chrome to the top zone and activate zone targeting with the right button; repeat after restart without a crash.
Verify existing layouts remain intact after restart and that aborted drags do not save corrupt zone assignments.
Repeat monitor/work-area changes during a drag only as a maintainer diagnostic discriminator, not as a claimed reporter step.

confidence.rationale: The crash path and existing safeguards need direct comparison; public symptoms alone cannot identify an omitted lifetime check.

issue_context.summary: A long-running FancyZones snapping crash report gained a linked 0.81.1 diagnostic report with a specific Chrome/right-button drag sequence.
known_information: The original report mentions 0.45 and lost layouts after restart.
The 2024 reply points to a public diagnostic ZIP in #33343.
The linked report concerns dragging Chrome to a top zone after a laptop restart.
Both issue reports remain open; #13402 is unassigned.
inferences: The linked report may help isolate the same crash family, but shared symptoms do not prove a common exception or that the original layout loss has the same cause.
issue_context.analysis: The last author-side reply was evidence, not silence. Review the linked artifact before asking for a new report or proposing a guard that current code already contains.
initial_investigation: Read both comments and the original report, then read #33343 and its available discussion.
Checked both issue timelines: the inspected cross-reference links the reports, not a concrete PR.
Current upstream FancyZones.cpp already aborts active drag state before clearing work areas and handles destroyed dragged windows; these existing guards must not be re-proposed as absent.

reproduce.title: FancyZones top-zone crash comparison
reproduce.version_requirement: Use 0.81.1 as the linked baseline and compare a current supported build.
prerequisites: A FancyZones layout with a top zone
Preserve a copy of existing layout configuration before testing.
steps: 1. Inspect the public ZIP in #33343 for the exception/module and zone configuration; do not assume it matches #13402.
2. Restart the test machine, open Chrome and grab its title bar.
3. Drag toward the top zone and press the right mouse button while dragging, then drop.
4. Repeat on a current build, record any crash signature and confirm saved layouts survive restart.
reproduce.expected_result: Zone highlighting and snapping succeed without crashing or losing layouts; any failure is tied to an observed stack before selecting a fix.
